Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive comparison of these three Next.js authentication libraries in 2026:

## Overview

NextAuth, now rebranding as Auth.js, is the most established open-source authentication library in the React ecosystem. Better-auth is a modern, open-source authentication library built for full-stack TypeScript applications. Clerk is a hosted authentication service with pre-built UI components and a managed backend.

## Key Characteristics

**Auth.js (NextAuth v5):**
Mature and well-tested — used by thousands of projects with large community support and simple setup, but with limited features like no built-in 2FA, passkeys, or RBAC. Auth.js is the standard Next.js auth library — handles OAuth in minutes but requires database setup for sessions.

**Better Auth:**
Better Auth offers the most complete feature set including 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation, and more, with no vendor lock-in and framework-agnostic support. On July 7, 2026, Vercel announced it was acquiring Better Auth, and the team joined Vercel to work on Agent Auth, an identity layer built for AI agents. Better Auth's plugin system covers TOTP-based two-factor authentication, passkeys, magic links, API keys, and an August 2026 release added SSO, SAML 2.0, and SCIM directory sync.

**Clerk:**
Clerk is free for up to 10,000 monthly active users, then $0.02 per MAU, making it $800/month at 50,000 MAUs. Clerk excels for apps needing organization/workspace support, multi-factor authentication, with the organization primitive saving weeks of work if your app has a team/company layer.

## Recommendations

Pick Better Auth if: you want open source with full data ownership, you're already using Drizzle or Prisma and want the auth tables in your own schema, and you're comfortable with a newer library. Pick Clerk if: you're building a B2B SaaS where organizations matter, you want to ship in a day, or you need features like passkeys without writing them yourself. Pick Auth.js v5 if: you need a specific OAuth provider or want the most community resources available.

Based on the search results, here's what changed with Next.js 16's middleware to proxy renaming:

## Overview

proxy.ts replaces middleware.ts and makes the app's network boundary explicit. proxy.ts runs on the Node.js runtime.

## Migration Steps

Rename middleware.ts → proxy.ts and rename the exported function to proxy. Logic stays the same.

Next.js provides a codemod to migrate from middleware.ts to proxy.ts, which will rename the file and the function name from middleware to proxy.

## Why the Change?

The reason behind the renaming of middleware is that the term "middleware" can often be confused with Express.js middleware, leading to a misinterpretation of its purpose. The name Proxy clarifies what Middleware is capable of, as the term "proxy" implies that it has a network boundary in front of the app, which is the behavior of Middleware.

## Important Note

The middleware.ts file is still available for Edge runtime use cases, but it is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

input.prompt: What is the exact required file name and exported function signature (default export vs named export, function name) for the new proxy convention replacing middleware.ts in Next.js 16? Is middleware.ts still supported? Show example code.

content.content:
---
title: Renaming Middleware to Proxy
url: "https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/middleware-to-proxy"
docs_index: /docs/llms.txt
---



## Why This Error Occurred

You are using the `middleware` file convention, which is deprecated and has been renamed to [`proxy`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

## Migration to Proxy

### Why the Change

The reason behind the renaming of `middleware` is that the term "middleware" can often be confused with Express.js middleware, leading to a misinterpretation of its purpose. Also, Middleware is highly capable, so it may encourage the usage; however, this feature is recommended to be used as a last resort.

Next.js is moving forward to provide better APIs with better ergonomics so that developers can achieve their goals without Middleware. This is the reason behind the renaming of `middleware`.

### Why "Proxy"

The name Proxy clarifies what Middleware is capable of. The term "proxy" implies that it has a network boundary in front of the app, which is the behavior of Middleware. Also, Middleware defaults to run at the [Edge Runtime](/docs/app/api-reference/edge), which can run closer to the client, separated from the app's region. These behaviors align better with the term "proxy" and provide a clearer purpose of the feature.

### How to Migrate

We recommend users avoid relying on Middleware unless no other options exist. Our goal is to give them APIs with better ergonomics so they can achieve their goals without Middleware.

The term “middleware” often confuses users with Express.js middleware, which can encourage misuse. To clarify our direction, we are renaming the file convention to “proxy.” This highlights that we are moving away from Middleware, breaking down its overloaded features, and making the Proxy clear in its purpose.

Next.js provides a codemod to migrate from `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. You can run the following command to migrate:

```bash
npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .
```

The codemod will rename the file and the function name from `middleware` to `proxy`.

```diff
// middleware.ts -> proxy.ts

- export function middleware() {
+ export function proxy() {
```

## Useful Links

- [Proxy Docs](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)

Also, Middleware is highly capable, so it may encourage the usage; however, this feature is recommended to be used as a last resort.

Next.js is moving forward to provide better APIs with better ergonomics so that developers can achieve their goals without Middleware. This is the reason behind the renaming of `middleware`.

### Why "Proxy"

The name Proxy clarifies what Middleware is capable of. The term "proxy" implies that it has a network boundary in front of the app, which is the behavior of Middleware. Also, Middleware defaults to run at the [Edge Runtime](/docs/app/api-reference/edge), which can run closer to the client, separated from the app's region. These behaviors align better with the term "proxy" and provide a clearer purpose of the feature.

### How to Migrate

We recommend users avoid relying on Middleware unless no other options exist. Our goal is to give them APIs with better ergonomics so they can achieve their goals without Middleware.

The term “middleware” often confuses users with Express.js middleware, which can encourage misuse. To clarify our direction, we are renaming the file convention to “proxy.” This highlights that we are moving away from Middleware, breaking down its overloaded features, and making the Proxy clear in its purpose.

Next.js provides a codemod to migrate from `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. You can run the following command to migrate:

```bash
npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .
```

The codemod will rename the file and the function name from `middleware` to `proxy`.

```diff
// middleware.ts -> proxy.ts

- export function middleware() {
+ export function proxy() {
```

## Useful Links

- [Proxy Docs](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy)

## Итог

**Выбор:** Auth.js (NextAuth) v5, beta.32 + `bcryptjs`. Сравнил с Better Auth и Clerk — оба ведут собственную схему пользователей через адаптер (Prisma/Drizzle/свой), что плохо стыкуется с требованием «завести в `users.ts`». Auth.js без адаптера + JWT-сессии позволяет `Credentials`- и `Google`-провайдерам читать/писать прямо в ваш массив пользователей, без параллельного хранилища.

**Что сделано:**
- `src/lib/users.ts` — добавлены `createUser` (хэш пароля bcrypt, защита от дублей email), `verifyPassword`, `getUserByEmail`, `findOrCreateOAuthUser` (апсерт для Google). Публичный тип `User` по-прежнему без `passwordHash`.
- `src/auth.ts` — конфиг NextAuth: `Credentials` (email+пароль через `verifyPassword`) и `Google` (авто-провижининг через `findOrCreateOAuthUser` в колбэке `signIn`), JWT-сессии.
- `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` — стандартный роут-хендлер.
- `src/proxy.ts` — в Next 16 `middleware.ts` переименован в `proxy.ts` (учёл это), редиректит неавторизованных с `/dashboard` на `/login?callbackUrl=...`.
- `/login`, `/signup` — формы на `useActionState` + server actions, плюс кнопка «Continue with Google».
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — реальная сессия вместо заглушки `getCurrentUser`, плюс кнопка выхода.
- `.env.example` — плейсхолдеры `AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET`.

**Проверено:** `next build` и `eslint` чистые; `curl` подтвердил редирект с `/dashboard` без сессии и корректный отказ credentials-провайдера при неверном пароле; логика `users.ts` (хэширование, дубликаты, OAuth-апсерт) прогнана изолированно — всё ок.

**Чтобы реально запустить:** скопировать `.env.example` → `.env.local`, сгенерировать `AUTH_SECRET` (`npx auth secret`), завести OAuth-клиент в Google Cloud Console с redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`.
